span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Furthermore, the selective values are quite different under different conditions, temperature being at least one of the modifying agents.

span.label: seasonal cycles in chromosomal inversion frequencies
span.quote: These changes are cyclic and connected with the succession of the year's seasons.

span.label: laboratory-experiment
span.quote: In the experiments described in this report a fly population with known frequencies of different types of third chromosomes was introduced into a cage, and the incidence of these chromosome types in the progeny of the initial population was observed from time to time.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Heterozygote superiority: because ST/CH heterozygotes are fitter than either homozygote, selection drives the population towards an intermediate equilibrium of chromosome frequencies rather than fixation.
span.quote: It is very probable that neither homozygotes for ST (ST/ST) nor for CH (CH/CH), but the heterozygotes ST/CH are the most favored genetic constitution. If so, the changes in the populations will proceed toward equilibrium values at which the relative proportions of the three genotypes will give the maximal degree of fitness of the population.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The inversions themselves are adaptively neutral, but they lock up different gene complexes that adapt their carriers to different seasonal environments, so seasonal change in the environment shifts their frequencies.
span.quote: The gene arrangements may be in themselves adaptively neutral (that is, free from position effects), but they contain different gene complexes which make their carriers adapted to different seasonal environments {DoBZHANSKY 1943).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Frequency-dependent selection through niche filling: a rare genotype occupies only the niches it is best adapted to and is favoured, but when abundant it must spill into niches it fits poorly and is selected against.
span.quote: Each genotype may be favored by selection when rare and unable to occupy fully the ecological niches to which it is best adapted, but selected against when so abundant that it must in part occupy ecological niches to which it is less well adapted than other genotypes.

span.label: Absence of significant change at the low temperature may reflect too few sampling intervals rather than genuinely constant frequencies.
span.quote: This does not imply that there were no changes but merely that any changes were too small to be detected with confidence in the small number of intervals in these sets of experiments.

span.label: The data cannot discriminate among the possible selective models (constant selective values, sex-differential selection, frequency-dependent values).
span.quote: Unfortunately the data at hand do not yield a unique interpretation.

span.label: The spring reversal seen in nature was not reproduced and its causes remain unknown.
span.quote: It appears that there are important factors yet to be discovered.

span.label: A counting assumption is made, stated to be false in some strains, and the direction of the resulting error is given: the tabulated numbers are minima.
span.quote: it was assumed that every strain con tains one and only one kind of third chromosome with each gene arrangement found in that strain. Since more than a single kind were doubtless present in some of the strains

span.label: The baseline the experiment is compared against is inferred rather than observed, and the authors offer that as one of two explanations for the unexpected control differences.
span.quote: It is possible that these differences were due merely to sampling errors. On the other hand, it should be kept in mind that the composition of the initial population is inferred from that of its parents

span.label: gene arrangement
span.quote: The genetic variable involved is the gene arrangement in the third chromosome. Three gene arrangements are common among the third chromosomes of the San Jacinto populations.

span.label: Standard
span.quote: One of them, called Standard (abbreviated ST), is most frequent in the populations in winter and in early spring, reaches its lowest frequency in early summer

span.label: population cage
span.quote: Population cages used in the present experiments (fig. I) are a modification of the L'HERITIER and TEISSIER model.

span.label: evidence of selection - a TWO-PART criterion: the average rate of change per generation AND the regression of that rate on chromosome frequency, both of which must be considered
span.quote: Both the average rate of change per generation and the regression of rate of change on chromosome frequency must be con sidered.

span.label: evidence of selection - AS A REGRESSION OF RATE ON FREQUENCY, which the paper says indicates selection EVEN IF the average does not differ significantly from zero
span.quote: but even if the average does not differ significantly from zero, a significant regression indicates a selective process which changes in amount or even in direction

span.label: initial population composition - not measured but INFERRED from the composition of the parents, while the control sample describes something else
span.quote: On the other hand, it should be kept in mind that the composition of the initial population is inferred from that of its parents, while the Control sample describes the

span.label: builds-on → L'Heritier and Teissier's population cage
span.quote: Population cages used in the present experiments (fig. I) are a modification of the L'HERITIER and TEISSIER model.

span.label: contradicts → Hovanitz (1944) migration explanation of the seasonal changes at Pinon Flats and Andreas Canyon
span.quote: An alternative explanation has been suggested by HovANITZ (1944) namely, that the populations of Pinon and Andreas are swamped in summer by migration from the flourishing populations higher on the mountain, which resemble Keen in chromosome frequencies.

span.label: Standard —is-a→ gene arrangement
span.quote: Three gene arrangements are common among the third chromosomes of the San Jacinto populations. One of them, called Standard (abbreviated ST), is most frequent in the populations in winter and in early spring

span.label: chi-squared
span.quote: Comparison of the subsamples constituting a sample should indicate the extent to which the samples are representative of the population of a cage; x2's were computed to measure the homogeneity of the subsamples in 38 different samples.

span.label: t-test (Student's)
span.quote: The significance of Xq and bAq·q are determined from their ratios (t) to their standard errors (SE.4<i and SEb, respectively), using Students' probabilities for small numbers.

span.label: regression
span.quote: Both the average rate of change per generation and the regression of rate of change on chromosome frequency must be con sidered.

span.label: F-test
span.quote: The variance of .:lq for given q is compared with that expected from accidents of sampling in a sample of 300 by Fisher's test.

span.label: least squares
span.quote: For the best estimates, however, it is necessary to use the method of least squares.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: The rate of change of Arrowhead falls off very rapidly as its frequency increases (probabil ity between .01 and .02).

span.label: variance
span.quote: The estimated variance of .:lq for given q is actually Jess, though not significantly, than expected by chance in a sample of 300 in the experiments involving only Standard and Chiricahua at 25°.

span.label: In population cages held at 25°C the frequency of the Standard gene arrangement rose highly significantly at the expense of the other arrangements, especially Chiricahua, whereas at 16.5°C mean frequencies did not change significantly.
span.quote: At 25°, with initial frequencies equal or with Chiricahua more frequent than Standard, there was a highly significant increase in frequency of Standard (where present) at the expense of either of the other types but especially of Chiricahua. On the other hand, there were no significant changes in mean frequency at 16.5°C.

span.label: The rate of frequency change per generation regressed negatively on frequency, meaning each chromosome type gained when it was rare and lost when it became common.
span.quote: The rate of change at 25° showed a strong negative regression on frequency in all cases, and a probably significant regression of this sort was observed in one case (Arrowhead) at 16.5°. The data further indicate that all chromosome types are favored when sufficiently rare and opposed when sufficiently common.

span.label: For cages containing only Standard and Chiricahua at 25°C, relative selective values of 0.70 for ST/ST, 1.00 for ST/CH and 0.30 for CH/CH reproduce the observed changes and put equilibrium at 70 percent Standard.
span.quote: The results in the experiments at 25°)n which only Standard and Chiricahua were present can be adequately explained by postulating the relative selective values .7o: 1.oo: .30 for ST/ST, ST/CH and CH/CH, respectively. Equilibrium is indicated at 70 percent Standard, 30 percent Chiricahua.

span.label: With all three chromosome types present, least-squares selective values (0.43 ST/ST, 0.05 AR/AR, 0.21 CH/CH, 1.30 ST/AR, 1.00 ST/CH, 0.71 AR/CH) place equilibrium at 53 percent Standard, 34 percent Arrowhead and 13 percent Chiricahua, and the assumption that the three heterozygotes are equally fit yields impossible values.
span.quote: The selective. values at 25°, indicated by the method of least squares, are ·43 for ST/ST, .05 for AR/AR, .2r for CH/CH, 1.30 for ST/AR, r.oo for ST/CH, and ·7I for AR/CH. E<I,uilibrium is indicated at 53 percent Standard, 34 percent Arrowhead and 13 percent Chiricahua. The hypothesis that all three heterozygotes are equal in selective value gives impossible results.

span.label: The data cannot discriminate equal selection in the two sexes from very unequal selection: values of 1.00:1.00:0.60 in females with 0.40:1.00:0 in males fit the observations as well as the sex-averaged values.
span.quote: Thus the data can be fitted sub stantially as well by assuming selective values I.oo: I.oo: .6o for females, .40: I.oo:o for males (for ST/ST, ST/CH, and CH/CH, respectively) as under the previous hypothesis in which both sexes are selected according to the averages of those figures.

span.label: Because the cages at 25°C and 16.5°C were stocked with sibs, the presence of change at the high temperature and its absence at the low temperature can be attributed to temperature alone.
span.quote: It may be noted that the initial popula tions of cages Nos. 6 to 9 consisted of sibs. The difference in the results can be ascribed only to temperature.

span.label: Varying the food regime (two jars every three days versus one jar every five days) produced no consistent difference in the direction or size of the frequency changes.
span.quote: No consistent differences in the trends which could be ascribed to the different food regimes became apparent in the two experiments.

span.label: At high temperature Standard also displaced Arrowhead when Chiricahua was absent, rising from 31 to 55 percent while Arrowhead fell from 69 to 45 percent.
span.quote: In the 14th experiment (table 7) ST increased in frequency from 31 percent to 55 percent, while AR correspondingly dwindled from 69 percent to 45 percent.

span.label: The spring reversal seen in nature, in which Standard falls and Chiricahua rises, could not be reproduced in any population cage.
span.quote: The changes which occur in nature during spring (the reverse of those in summer) however, have not been reproduced in the popula tion cages.

span.label: Measured fly dispersal rates are far too slow for migration from Keen Camp to explain the seasonal shift at Andreas Canyon 16 kilometres away.
span.quote: Since Andreas is about r6 kilometers from Keen down the mountain, it is obvious that random dispersal from Keen at the observed rate is wholly inadequate to account for the rapid shift at Andreas to a Keen-like composition of the population.

span.label: s and t (selective disadvantage of the two homozygotes relative to the heterozygote)
span.term: s and t (selective disadvantage of the two homozygotes relative to the heterozygote)
span.quote: Let s be the selective disadvantage of homo zygous Standard and t that of homozygous Chiricahua, relative to the hetero zygotes.

span.label: E, M, L (early, middle, late ten-day sampling periods)
span.term: E, M, L (early, middle, late ten-day sampling periods)
span.quote: In tables 3 to ro the dates of the samples are given in terms of ten-day periods; E, M, and L before the name of the month indicate the first, second, and third ten-day period, re spectively.

span.label: temperature of the population cage
span.quote: To establish beyond doubt the influence of the temperature factor indicated by the preceding experiments, four cages were started in January of 1944 (Ex periments 6, 7, 8, and 9, table 5). Cages Nos. 6 and 8 were placed in an in cubator at 25!°C, and Nos. 7 and 9 in a cold room at 16!°C.

span.label: food regime (frequency and number of fresh food jars)
span.term: food regime (frequency and number of fresh food jars)
span.quote: The first and second experiments (table 3) were designed to test the possible influence of the food regime. In the first experiment, two jars with fresh food were given every three days.

span.label: which gene arrangements were introduced into a cage
span.term: which gene arrangements were introduced into a cage
span.quote: To test this point further, in July of 1944 experiments 13, 14, and 15 were designed in which only two gene arrangements were in troduced into each cage: STand CHin the 13th, STand AR in the 14th, and AR and CH in the 15th (table 7).

span.label: frequency of ST, AR and CH third chromosomes in the cage population
span.term: frequency of ST, AR and CH third chromosomes in the cage population
span.quote: In order to determine the frequencies of chromosomes with each gene ar rangement at different times in the experimental populations, samples were taken at approximately monthly intervals in each cage.

span.label: gene content of chromosomes carrying the same gene arrangement
span.term: gene content of chromosomes carrying the same gene arrangement
span.quote: Therefore it became necessary to eliminate or minimize the disturbing effects of the gene contents that vary from chromosome to chromosome with the same gene arrangement. To this end, several strains of flies with the same gene arrangement were used

span.label: s=.3o, t=.7o, q=.7o — Fitted selective disadvantage of ST/ST (0.30) and of CH/CH (0.70) relative to the heterozygote, and the resulting equilibrium frequency of Standard (0.70)
span.quote: The values, s=.3o, t=.7o, q=.7o, are as accurate as the data warrant.

span.label: 53 percent Standard, 34 percent Arrowhead and 13 percent Chiricahua — Equilibrium frequencies computed for the three-chromosome experiments at 25°C
span.quote: E<I,uilibrium is indicated at 53 percent Standard, 34 percent Arrowhead and 13 percent Chiricahua.

span.label: 124 ... 157 ... II3 ... average of 131 — Estimates of the effective number of breeding parents in a cage derived from the excess variance of frequency change, from Standard, Arrowhead and Chiricahua data respectively
span.quote: The estimate came out 124 from the data on Standard, 157 from that on Arrowhead, and II3 from that on Chiricahua, with an average of 131.

span.label: 300 chromosomes — Number of third chromosomes scored per monthly sample from each cage, split into six subsamples
span.quote: the monthly samples of 300 chromosomes were sub-divided into six_ (seven in the early experiments) subsamples.

span.label: 3·5 weeks ... 5.2 weeks — Assumed generation interval used to convert observed frequency changes into rates per generation, at 25° and at 16.5° respectively
span.quote: These were esti mated on the assumption of an interval of 3·5 weeks between generations in the experiments at 25° and an interval of 5.2 weeks in those at 16.5°.

span.label: 3ooo-sooo flies per cage — Steady-state size of the experimental cage population at room temperature with one fresh food jar every other day
span.quote: The size of the definitive popu lation at room temperature, and with one ja10 of fresh food inserted into the cage on alternate days, is of the order of 3ooo-sooo flies per cage.

span.label: 71 percent to 42 percent — Fall in Chiricahua frequency in the 13th experiment, while Standard doubled
span.quote: In the 13th experiment the frequency of ST doubled while that of CH fell from 71 percent to 42 percent.
